evidence.source: Wu Yuanyuan, Zhengzhou University Center for Chinese Characters Civilization Research
evidence.field: §2.1.1 商朝数词{三}的用字；甲骨文合集 H.16189, H.37453
evidence.text: The study reports 三 used for the numeral in Shang oracle-bone corpus examples H.16189 and H.37453, and says 三 was the only graph slot it found for the numeral in Shang sources. The cited examples have no precise inscription date in the article.
evidence.title: 数词﹛三﹜的用字演变研究（一）

evidence.source: Wu Yuanyuan, Zhengzhou University Center for Chinese Characters Civilization Research
evidence.field: §2.1.2–2.2; Zhou, Warring States, and Qin-Han numeral spellings
evidence.text: The study reports 三 alongside 參 for the numeral in Zhou sources, with a cited Western Zhou late bronze example; it reports 品/晶 among Warring States Chu manuscript spellings and 三 and 參 in excavated Qin-Han texts. These are alternate graphs for the numeral, not evidence that 三 itself was borrowed from another word. The author excludes one transmitted Hanshu instance of 叄 from the Qin-Han count as possibly due to later substitution; that is a qualified proposal, not proof the form was impossible then.
evidence.kind: scholarly report of historical orthographic use and qualified textual assessment
evidence.title: 数词﹛三﹜的用字演变研究（一）

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Institute of History and Philology, Xiaoxuetang
evidence.field: 字形演變; 集成04261; 楚系簡帛文字; 小篆; 說文
evidence.text: The entry identifies U+4E09 and lists a bronze-script record 集成04261, Chu manuscript forms, and a Small Seal form. It explains the three equal horizontal strokes as three equal counting rods representing three. Its text does not establish that the earliest graph was directly devised by copying physical rods.
evidence.title: 漢字「三」：字形演變

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, transcription of Shuowen Jiezi with Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.field: 三 entry; 許慎 text and 段玉裁《說文解字注》
evidence.text: The transmitted Shuowen account says 三 is “the way of Heaven, Earth, and humanity” and says it is formed “from the number three”; it records 弎 as an ancient form written with 弋. Duan Yucai comments that the three strokes embody the three powers. This later lexicographic interpretation is distinct from the counting-rod explanation and does not independently attest the Shang graph.
evidence.title: 說文解字「三」

gaps: No original oracle-bone or bronze facsimile was independently inspected; the Shang numeral examples are reported by the scholarly survey without precise year or reign.
The counting-rod explanation is the paleographic entry's interpretation; direct derivation of the earliest graph from physical rods is not established.

The inspected evidence supports early numeral use and alternate numeral spellings, but does not establish a full dated chronology of secondary semantic extensions of the spoken numeral. No chronology is inferred from dictionary glosses.

No sound component or whole-graph phonetic loan is proposed. The possible influence of 四 in the supplied Baxter–Sagart spoken reconstruction does not establish graph formation; the dossier's Proto-Sino-Tibetan comparison was not independently assessed.
The official Unicode character-specific lookup for 三 was inaccessible. Its supplied local kMandarin row is sān; it is local evidence, not a verified current upstream page.

The exact Commons file pages and exact MediaWiki imageinfo API requests for both glyph leads could not be opened. No image pixels, historical label, file source, or exact reuse terms were independently verified, so neither lead is selected. The Commons category result only establishes that Shuowen Seal Radical 004.svg is listed there.
No repeated-source bulk extract is recommended: reuse permission and the value of a versioned extract were not established.
